metadata.history_order: oldest to newest; interval of length dt ending at each times entry
metadata.prediction_time: u,h and full prior drive record available before response o; o unavailable
metadata.matching: u and h are exact controlled values; histories intentionally differ
metadata.measurement_certificate: Evaluator supplies calibrated identical reference channel; absolute readout error bounded by 0.015 response units. Conditional development assumption, not inferred from repeated data.
metadata.fit_rule: refit all parameters on fit only; dev separate; all targets raw o
metadata.old_model_optimizer: unconstrained linear least squares global minimizer

language.syntax: Every expression is ONE pure expression, no assignment or semicolons. No literal lists, ranges, slicing, loops or row-dependent parameters. Use raw times instead of writing a time vector. Define quantities sequentially. All parameter names referenced must occur in parameters. Finite lower<initial<upper. Do NOT declare automatic linear response coefficients; declare only nonlinear parameters actually used in features/quantities. Tool infers units and creates output coefficients.
language.completion: You choose 1..4 scalar features and polynomial degree1..3. The tool may form powers/products of only those features and fits at most8 total parameters, including at most2 nonlinear parameters. It does not invent omitted inputs or history transformations.
language.experiments: u [-1.1,1.1], h [0,2.5], each history entry [-1,1]; only these inputs and scalar response can be measured. No internal sensor. New conditions must differ from all supplied observations. Up to2 pairs,4 repeats per condition, frozen forecasts before acquisition.

task: Discover a useful response representation from failed o=f(u,h), extending or replacing the function as supported by evidence. The current model is a previous failed agent proposal, not a required structure. Use concrete quantities and executable experiments.
acceptance: Raw response RMSE<=0.06 on dev, fresh hidden observations, random confirmation and each acquired intervention pair. Final independent targets cannot be used for revision.

experiment_choice.expected_distinction: E1 and E2 distinguish C0's claimed strong dependence on the most recent history interval from C1/C2, which predict no response contrast when only history[3] changes. However, both C1 and C2 omit history[3] from their actual executable fitted expression, so neither realizes its stated history proposal. C0 also fits the supplied development conditions poorly (RMSE 0.2784); none of these candidates is supported as an accepted representation.
experiment_choice.reason: Choose the two offered pairs that vary only history[3] while holding u, h, and the other history entries fixed. This directly tests a large contrast predicted by C0 against a zero contrast from the executable C1/C2 models. The evidence already shows history dependence and h-by-history variation in controlled observations, but does not establish a complete response law; these interventions test a specific distinction without treating tool predictions as scientific support.
experiment_choice.revision_if_refuted: If the observed history[3] contrasts do not match C0 within measurement tolerance, reject C0's recent-interval effect. Refit on fit only with explicitly specified history coordinates and waiting-time-by-history terms, then evaluate on fresh held-out conditions; do not claim acceptance unless raw dev, fresh hidden, random-confirmation, and each acquired intervention-pair targets meet the stated RMSE criterion.

scientific_proposal.label: Signed history product with current and recent inputs
scientific_proposal.prospective_contrast: At fixed u=0.3 and h=0.5, contrast histories [1,0,0,0] and [0,0,0,1], then repeat at h=1.5. Their measured means differ by about 0.301 at h=0.5 and 0.190 at h=1.5; the endpoint history term alone cannot explain this, motivating tests of earlier versus later history contributions.
scientific_proposal.refutation_condition: Refit on fit only; reject if raw dev RMSE exceeds 0.06 or if frozen predictions miss either fresh intervention-pair mean by more than the 0.06 criterion.
scientific_proposal.scientific_change: Replace the failed u,h-only response with explicit dependence on the oldest interval and a nonlinear interaction of the interior history intervals, while retaining u and h.

scientific_proposal.label: History shape with waiting-time modulation
scientific_proposal.prospective_contrast: At u=0.65, compare the same histories [1,0,0,0] and [0,0,0,1] at h=0.5 versus h=2.2: the observed endpoint-history contrast changes from roughly 0.292 to 0.135. The model predicts only an h main effect, so acquire a new matched pair with mixed-sign histories at both waiting times to test for h-by-history interaction.
scientific_proposal.refutation_condition: The proposal is inadequate if fit-only refitting gives dev RMSE above 0.06 or frozen predictions fail the new mixed-sign pair contrasts beyond 0.06 response units.
scientific_proposal.scientific_change: Test the parsimonious additive history account first; the waiting-time dependence of the observed history contrast motivates a later interaction extension if this account fails.

instruction: Use the NEW experiment results to propose up to TWO revised representations. Explain which empirical distinction each revision preserves and what the observations actually refute. A fixed fitted formula failing does not refute an entire feature class unless a scoped collision certificate proves it. Each proposal is checked against old evidence AND each active pair before response search; provably insufficient representations cannot be completed. Preserve all already supported distinctions. All parameters must be declared and the claimed kernel family must agree with the mathematical operators.
